original.target_description: Control analysis: biserial correlation of edible high-calorie food versus non-food ball object type with valence ratings.

n.sample_role: Analytic rating/observation unit and N not explicitly stated for the biserial correlation; 20 participants contributed to the study.
n.exclusions: One male excluded for hand tracking difficulty; two female datasets lost technically; correlation-specific missingness or aggregation not stated.
n.location: manuscript pp. 7, 9, 12, object ratings; final sample; control analysis
n.quote:
One male participant was not comfortable with the hand tracking procedure and

repeatedly failed in positioning the starting hand. Two female participant’s data were lost

due to technical problems. Data are reported for the remaining 20 participants. ... As expected, there was a trend for edible objects to be rated more positively than

ball objects, though the biserial correlation of object type and valence ratings was rather

small, r=.15, p=.059.
